decisions.reason: The replication title revisits the effect of internationalization on firm governance, which matches Sanders and Carpenter (1998) in the supplied reference list and confirms the shipped original.

parent_objection: Source contains only title, empty Abstract heading and publisher reference list, no empirical methods/results or named tested original. First reply certifies replication from title alone and original identity from one similarly titled reference. Step1 distinguishes new-data replication from original-data reproduction or plans; title Replication and Extension does not establish data relationship. Step2 prohibits inferring target merely from title/topic/bibliography unless exactly one citation fits the described finding. Does supplied source actually describe an original finding or identify Sanders/Carpenter as retested, or are type and identity unverified? Reassess all3fields independently using available source; do not treat absence of contradiction as confirmation or shipped/blind agreement as evidence. Outcome remains unsupported. Return explicit uncertainty where source cannot establish relationship.

shipped.title_o: INTERNATIONALIZATION AND FIRM GOVERNANCE: THE ROLES OF CEO COMPENSATION, TOP TEAM COMPOSITION, AND BOARD STRUCTURE.
shipped.outcome_quote: Our results find general support for Sanders and Carpenter’s (1998) central premise that internationalization shapes firm governance structures but also highlight important non-findings that reflect how the internationalization-governance relationship has changed since their study.

blind_target.authors: Sanders, W. G., & Carpenter, M. A.
blind_target.title: Internationalization and firm governance: The roles of CEO compensation, top team composition, and board structure.
blind_target.evidence_quote: Given that firm governance structures have substantially changed over the past few decades, our study revisits these relationships by conducting a replication of Sanders and Carpenter (1998).
blind_target.outcome_quote: Our results find general support for Sanders and Carpenter’s (1998) central premise that internationalization shapes firm governance structures but also highlight important non-findings that reflect how the internationalization-governance relationship has changed since their study.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly present support alongside non-replicated findings; the general premise alone is not an overall successful replication verdict.
